corrections.old:
For the serving assembly — `handle` and its region functions — and the exchange machine it
drives:

Every `ExchangeEvent` the machine learns of reaches it in one of exactly two ways. A
STAGE-OWNED event travels inside an `Established<T>`: the carrier is constructed at the site
the stage's work returned its product, has no public field and no reader other than
`ExchangeProgress::establish` and, for the notification terminal's carrier,
`ServedSuccess::tail`, which reads its event alone — for `may_publish` to check before the 202
is signed and for `publish` to advance after the outcome commitment and retention, the product
never yielded — and is `#[must_use]`, so the assembly cannot obtain the product without the
machine advancing the event in the same step and cannot discard the product without a warning
the build refuses. An
ASSEMBLY-OWNED event is stated by a direct `advance` in the serving path, and the set of events
stated that way is exactly the three inventoried with the reason no stage's success could carry
each: `BackendDispatched`, `ContinuationRetired`, `ContinuationNotRequired`. The success tail —
`EvidenceRetained`, then `TerminalResponseServed` or `OpenLegResponseServed` — is advanced only
by `PublishPermit::publish`, after `may_publish` has checked the same tail, and the serving
path advances none of them itself.

The two sets are disjoint: no event a stage establishes is also advanced by the serving path,
so no stage's fact is stated twice or remembered beside the carrier. The assembly-owned set is
measured in both directions — an advance naming an event outside the three, and a listed event
the serving path no longer advances, are each a failing control — so a deleted assembly-owned
`advance` is detected, not merely forbidden.

Legality is THM-0043's: every advance, by either route, is checked against the relation in
every build and latches an anomaly when refused. What this theorem adds is that for the
stage-owned events the machine's state implies the stage's product was obtained, and for the
three it names, and only those, the correspondence rests on the assembly's own statement.
corrections.new:
For the serving assembly — `handle` and its region functions — and the exchange machine it
drives:

Every `ExchangeEvent` the machine declares reaches it by exactly one of four routes. A
STAGE-OWNED event travels inside an `Established<T>`: the carrier is constructed at the site
the stage's work returned its product, has no public field and no reader other than
`ExchangeProgress::establish` and, for the notification terminal's carrier,
`ServedSuccess::tail`, which reads its event alone — for `may_publish` to check before the 202
is signed and for `publish` to advance after the outcome commitment and retention, the product
never yielded — and is `#[must_use]`, so the assembly cannot obtain the product without the
machine advancing the event in the same step and cannot discard the product without a warning
the build refuses. An
ASSEMBLY-OWNED event is stated by a direct `advance` in the serving path, and the set of events
stated that way is exactly the three inventoried with the reason no stage's success could carry
each: `BackendDispatched`, `ContinuationRetired`, `ContinuationNotRequired`. The success tail —
`EvidenceRetained`, then `TerminalResponseServed` or `OpenLegResponseServed` — is advanced only
by `PublishPermit::publish`, after `may_publish` has checked the same tail, and the serving
path advances none of them itself. The REFUSAL terminal, `Refused`, is entered only by
`ExchangeProgress::refuse`, which the crate calls at one site, `disposition`, where a
refusal's retry contract is read from the machine: it states no stage's work, it is not one of
the assembly's three, and which terminal it reaches, refused before the dispatch or failed
after it, is the relation's answer and not the caller's.

The routes partition the events the machine declares: each event is on exactly one, so no
stage's fact is stated twice or remembered beside the carrier, and no event reaches the machine
by a route nothing measures. The assembly-owned set is measured in both directions — an advance
naming an event outside the three, and a listed event the serving path no longer advances, are
each a failing control — so a deleted assembly-owned `advance` is detected, not merely
forbidden. The refusal entry is measured the same way: a refusal entered anywhere else in the
crate, and a `disposition` that no longer refuses, are each a failing control.

Legality is THM-0043's: every advance, by any route, is checked against the relation in every
build and latches an anomaly when refused. What this theorem adds is that for the stage-owned
events the machine's state implies the stage's product was obtained, and for the three it
names, and only those, the correspondence rests on the assembly's own statement. The refusal
terminal carries no correspondence claim: what is claimed for it is its single entry.
corrections.reason: #1277 made every refusal enter its terminal through ExchangeProgress::refuse, called from disposition. The statement's 'exactly two ways' was false: the publication tail was a third route and Refused was on none. The statement now partitions every declared event over four routes, names the refusal route with its single entry, and keeps the stage-establishment and publication clauses byte-identical. Controls: exchange_transition_ownership_test::every_exchange_event_reaches_the_machine_by_exactly_one_route, ::the_refusal_terminal_is_entered_only_by_refuse_from_the_disposition, ::the_refusal_rule_would_catch_an_unauthorized_entry.

corrections.old:
The serving assembly under `http_profile_serve/` and the carrier in `exchange_state.rs`,
production halves only. The three assembly-owned transitions are EXCLUDED from the
correspondence claim: that the dispatch and the two continuation facts are stated at the right
moment is the assembly's own statement, read by hand, and this theorem says only that those
three are the whole residue and that removing one is detected. The publication tail's
correspondence is the cross-machine invariant's (`exchange_publication`). Not stated: that a
stage's work is correct (each stage's own theorem), that the relation is complete (THM-0043),
or that a refusal carries the right disposition (THM-0081).

`Established` is constructible anywhere in the crate; the claim is not that a wrong carrier is
unconstructible but that every carrier in the serving path is built at its stage's success site
(source-measured, listed in the packet) and that nothing but `establish` can open one, and
nothing but `establish` and `ServedSuccess::tail` reads one (structural). Source-text evidence,
recorded as evidence: deleting the battery leaves a reintroduced `advance` compiling. Class V0.
corrections.new:
The serving assembly under `http_profile_serve/` and the carrier in `exchange_state.rs`,
production halves only; the refusal entry is measured over the crate's production source
outside the machine, because `refuse` is visible crate-wide. The three assembly-owned transitions are EXCLUDED from the
correspondence claim: that the dispatch and the two continuation facts are stated at the right
moment is the assembly's own statement, read by hand, and this theorem says only that those
three are the whole residue and that removing one is detected. The publication tail's
correspondence is the cross-machine invariant's (`exchange_publication`). Not stated: that a
stage's work is correct (each stage's own theorem), that the relation is complete (THM-0043),
that a refusal carries the right disposition (THM-0081), or that every refusal the serving
path serves derives its disposition through `disposition` and so enters the terminal
(refusal-site totality, THM-0081's evidence).

`Established` is constructible anywhere in the crate; the claim is not that a wrong carrier is
unconstructible but that every carrier in the serving path is built at its stage's success site
(source-measured, listed in the packet) and that nothing but `establish` can open one, and
nothing but `establish` and `ServedSuccess::tail` reads one (structural). Source-text evidence,
recorded as evidence: deleting the battery leaves a reintroduced `advance` compiling, and a
refusal entered through an alias or a macro is outside a source scan. Class V0.
corrections.reason: The refusal entry is measured over the crate's production source outside the machine, because refuse is pub(crate). The scope now says so, lists refusal-site totality as not stated here (THM-0081's evidence), and names an alias or macro call as outside a source scan.

reason: PRECISION. The reviewed statement misdescribed the event routes after #1277. The correction states the route the code already has and adds the control that measures it. The security consequence, severity, depends_on, support and review requirement are byte-identical, and the stage-owned, assembly-owned and publication-tail clauses are unchanged.
ruling: ADR-MCPRE-068 Phase-1 campaign ruling, 2026-09-18: a correction of a statement that misdescribes what production establishes, leaving the accepted promise intact, is not an owner escalation. Prepared on the owner's direction of 2026-11-04 to correct THM-0101 for the refusal route. A correction record is not an approval: it does not make the specification-review axis fresh, and release-mode establishment still asks for the owner, who decides whether the refusal-entry clause is precision or expansion.
